module purpose: A parameterizable FIFO buffer: it accepts write data and write-enable inputs, stores entries in an internal register or memory depending on FIFO_DEPTH, updates write/read pointers on clk_i, and presents read data and occupancy/status outputs (free_o, avail_o, half_o, level_o). Behavior is configurable by generics FIFO_RSYNC (synchronous read), FIFO_SAFE (gate enables) and FULL_RESET (memory reset).

use-case flows.value: Write: a write request (we_i) causes wdata_i to be written into FIFO storage and advances the write pointer
Read: a read request (re_i) causes the read pointer to advance and the selected stored entry to be presented on rdata_o
Pointer and occupancy update: w_pnt/r_pnt are clocked, w_nxt/r_nxt are computed (including clear_i), and level/match/full/empty/half are derived from the pointers
Stored entry returned on rdata_o: read logic selects fifo_mem or fifo_reg at the current read index and drives rdata_o (sync or async depending on FIFO_RSYNC)
Status reporting: free/avail/half are produced and copied to free_o/avail_o/half_o, and level is extended to level_o (synchronously or combinationally depending on FIFO_RSYNC)
Reset clears pointer registers (and, when FULL_RESET is true, clears the memory/register contents and resets status outputs)

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO stored entries (the data values held in the FIFO memory or single-entry register that must be delivered unchanged on read)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Writes copy wdata_i into storage and later the same storage drives rdata_o: write processes assign fifo_reg/fifo_mem from wdata_i (RTL lines 135, 150, 171, 184) and read paths drive rdata_o from the same storage (RTL lines 201, 213, 232, 241). The relationship map shows wdata_i CARRIES into fifo_mem at occurrence 3 (line 150) and fifo_mem is CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3 (line 150); rdata_o DERIVES_FROM fifo_mem at occurrence 3 (line 213). Corrupting these stored values would make rdata_o differ from prior writes, so integrity of the stored entries is established by these assignments and connections.

conceptual assets.concept: Effective write-enable decision (the internal write-permit that actually gates storing an entry)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The internal write decision 'we' determines whether storage processes take wdata_i: the RTL assigns we from we_i (and free when FIFO_SAFE=true) (line 65) and the write processes are gated by we (e.g. 'if (we = '1') then fifo_reg/fifo_mem <= wdata_i' at lines 135, 150, 171, 184). The map records show we DERIVES_FROM we_i (occurrence 2, line 65) and we_i SOURCES we (occurrence 2, line 65), establishing the effective write enable as a computed decision the module depends on.

conceptual assets.concept: Effective read-enable decision (the internal read-permit that actually advances the read side and enables delivery)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The internal read decision 're' controls pointer advancement and which entry is presented: RTL assigns re from re_i (and avail when FIFO_SAFE=true) (line 64) and r_nxt/pointer advances and rdata_o use that decision (lines 77, 83, 207-213, 238-241). The map shows re DERIVES_FROM re_i at occurrence 2 (line 64) and re_i SOURCES re (occurrence 2, line 64), establishing the effective read enable as the decision the module uses.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO pointer state (the write and read pointers that determine which locations are written and read)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The stored-entry indexing and read/write behavior depend on the pointer registers: pointer_reg resets w_pnt/r_pnt and on clk_i updates w_pnt<=w_nxt and r_pnt<=r_nxt (lines 70-78); the write processes index fifo_mem using w_pnt (lines 150, 184) and read processes select fifo_mem using r_pnt or the registered r_pnt_ff (lines 213, 241). The map records show w_pnt CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3 (line 76) and r_pnt CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3 (line 77); r_pnt_ff is a stored delayed read pointer (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 2, line 210) used by async read. The pointer registers therefore realize the pointer-state concept whose integrity the FIFO relies on.

conceptual assets.concept: Occupancy/status indicators (free, avail, half) and their exported ports that gate operations and report FIFO state
conceptual assets.reasoning: Occupancy signals determine permitted operations and are exported to other blocks: free is computed as not full (line 110) and copied to free_o (line 217); avail is computed as not empty (line 111) and copied to avail_o (line 218); half is computed from level or full (line 96) and copied to half_o (lines 219/256). The map records show free DERIVES_FROM full at occurrence 3 (line 110) and free_o COPIES free at occurrence 2 (line 217); avail DERIVES_FROM empty at occurrence 3 (line 111) and avail_o COPIES avail at occurrence 2 (line 218); half is GATED_BY the 'level(...) or full' guard at occurrence 2 (line 96) and half_o COPIES half at occurrence 2 (line 219). Because writes/reads are gated by these signals (we uses free; re uses avail), their integrity is established by the RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: Level count (number of entries currently stored) and its exported readback
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes a numeric occupancy level (level <= unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt), line 95) and extends that value to the 32-bit level_o output (process level_extend lines 114-118). The map shows level DERIVES_FROM w_pnt (occurrence 2, line 95) and level_o DERIVES_FROM level (occurrence 3, line 117). The correctness of the level value matters to consumers and is established by these RTL computations and connections.

conceptual assets.concept: Clear request (the external clear_i input that forces pointers to zero and empties the FIFO)
conceptual assets.reasoning: clear_i, when asserted, forces w_nxt and r_nxt to (others => '0') (RTL lines 82-83). The map records clear_i GATES w_nxt at occurrence 2 (line 82) and GATES r_nxt at occurrence 3 (line 83); w_nxt/r_nxt are then carried into the pointer registers on the next clk edge (pointer_reg lines 70-78). Because clear_i directly empties the pointer state used to select memory entries, it is an availability-relevant control input established by the RTL.
